turns.text: I'm Tomas, engineering lead at Helix. We're migrating our data pipeline, codename Atlas, from Airflow to Dagster.
Main goal: finish the Atlas migration by the end of Q3. Help me keep track of blockers.
Team: Mei owns ingestion, Jonas owns the warehouse models, and Sara is our SRE.
Coffee machine on our floor broke again, morale is low, haha.
Blocker: the Snowflake connector for Dagster doesn't support our key-pair auth yet. Jonas is on it.
Secondary goal: cut pipeline run cost by 30% as part of the migration.
We use Snowflake as the warehouse and dbt for transformations; dbt runs are the expensive part.
What's a good book on management for first-time leads?
Who owns ingestion on my team?
Jonas got the key-pair auth working with a custom resource, so that blocker is gone.
New blocker: Sara says the Dagster deployment on our Kubernetes cluster needs a bigger node pool, approval pending from finance.
Do you have a recipe for a quick weeknight pasta?
Mei finished porting the ingestion DAGs; 40 of 40 done.
What's currently blocking Atlas?
Finance approved the node pool budget. Sara will provision it next week.
Add a goal: write a runbook for on-call before we switch over.
Is Dagster a public company?
We found that 60% of dbt cost comes from full refreshes of the orders model; Jonas is making it incremental.
Actually, scratch the Q3 deadline; leadership moved the Atlas cutover to mid-October.
When is the Atlas cutover now?
Any idea why my standing desk keeps drifting down?
Sara finished the node pool; Dagster is deployed to staging.
Jonas's incremental orders model cut dbt cost by 35%, so the cost goal is met.
Did we hit the cost reduction goal? Give me the number.
Remind me how to pronounce 'Dagster', is it dag-ster?
Mei is going on parental leave from next month; her ingestion work will be picked up by a new hire, Leo.
Who will own ingestion after next month?
What goals are still open for Atlas?
Who is our SRE and what did she deliver?
Summarise the Atlas project status in a few sentences.
